questions.q: A multi-task run failed. After fixing the code, which tasks does Repair run?

options.t: Only the unsuccessful tasks and their dependants, with the current settings
Only the failed task, with the settings of the failed run
options.why: Repair uses current settings and reruns dependants.

options.t: The tasks you pick, in any order
Every task in the job again, from the first, with the settings of the failed run

questions.explain: Repair re-runs only the unsuccessful tasks and their dependants, with the current job and task settings.

questions.q: A task appended half its output before failing. What happens on Repair?

options.t: Repair rolls back the partial write first
The task restarts and appends everything again, duplicating the first half
Repair refuses tasks that wrote data
Repair resumes the task from where it stopped, so nothing is written twice

questions.explain: A repaired task restarts from the beginning and isn't made idempotent; write with overwrite or MERGE so reruns are harmless.

questions.q: A job parameter `run_date` and a task parameter `run_date` both exist on a key-value task. Which wins?

options.t: The run fails with a conflict
The task parameter
The job parameter
The one set most recently in the UI

questions.explain: Job parameters are pushed down to key-value tasks, and when keys clash the job parameter takes precedence.

questions.q: A failed run must be repaired with a different `run_date`. Is that possible?

options.t: Only for task values
options.why: Task values are set by tasks.

options.t: No; parameters are fixed per run
options.why: You can override job parameters when repairing.

options.t: Only by editing the job's defaults and starting a brand-new run
Yes: job parameters can be overridden when repairing a run

questions.explain: You can override job parameters when running with different parameters, and when repairing a run.

questions.q: Which reference passes the run's start date (UTC) to a task?

options.t: `{{job.start_time.iso_date}}`
`{{now()}}`, evaluated at run time
`{{task.start_date}}`
`{{start_date}}`

questions.explain: {{job.start_time.<argument>}} gives a value from the run's start time in UTC, such as iso_date; {{start_date}} is deprecated.

questions.q: A parameter contains `{{job.runid}}` (a typo). What happens?

options.t: It is replaced by an empty string
It may be kept as the literal text; only invalid references in a known namespace raise an error
The job fails to start until the reference is corrected in the job settings
It resolves to the run ID anyway

questions.explain: Syntax errors and non-existent references are silently treated as literal strings; a reference in a known namespace that isn't valid shows an error.

questions.q: Which reference counts the times the current task has run, retries and repairs included?

options.t: `{{job.repair_count}}` for the job
options.why: That counts repair attempts of the run.

options.t: `{{task.run_id}}`
`{{task.execution_count}}`
`{{task_retry_count}}`

questions.explain: {{task.execution_count}} is the number of times the current task ran, including retries and repairs.

questions.q: Which `mode: production` checks does a bundle deployment run? (Choose two.)

options.t: The current Git branch matches the target's git.branch
run_as and permissions are specified
Schedules are paused
Resources get a [dev name] prefix
--cluster-id may override clusters

questions.explain: mode: production checks pipelines aren't in development, the Git branch matches, paths aren't user-specific, and run_as and permissions are set.

questions.q: A CI pipeline must pass a secret into a bundle variable without writing it in databricks.yml. How?

options.t: Store it in a tag on the job, read at deployment
Hard-code it in the notebook
Put it in the target's variables block
options.why: That writes it into the file.

options.t: Set the environment variable `BUNDLE_VAR_<name>`

questions.explain: Bundle variables can be given at run time with --var, a BUNDLE_VAR_<name> environment variable, or variable-overrides.json; secrets never go in databricks.yml.

questions.q: In the Databricks SDK for Python, which client lists a workspace's clusters?

options.t: `WorkspaceClient().clusters.list()`
`SparkSession.clusters()`
`dbutils.clusters.list()`
`AccountClient().clusters.list()` with an account token

questions.explain: WorkspaceClient serves workspace APIs (the page's example lists clusters); AccountClient serves account APIs such as groups.

questions.q: What authentication standard does the Databricks SDK for Python implement?

options.t: A separate login per API call
Databricks unified authentication: configure once, reuse across tools
Only hard-coded personal access tokens, passed to each client
options.why: Hard-coding is supported but not recommended.

options.t: Only Kerberos

questions.explain: The SDK implements Databricks unified authentication; hard-coding tokens is supported but not recommended.

questions.q: Where does Databricks discourage installing libraries?

options.t: A serverless environment
Unity Catalog volumes, which only admins can write
options.why: Volumes are the recommended place on DBR 13.3 LTS+.

options.t: DBFS, which any workspace user can write to
A compute policy's library list

questions.explain: Libraries in DBFS are writable by any user and are discouraged; on DBR 13.3 LTS+ with Unity Catalog, install from volumes.

questions.q: Which advice about init scripts is correct?

options.t: Use global scripts for everything
Install every library with them, so all nodes get the same versions
options.why: Never install libraries through init scripts.

options.t: Serverless supports them
Prefer platform features such as compute policies, and pin package versions

questions.explain: Databricks recommends platform features over init scripts, cluster-scoped over global, never installing libraries through them, and pinning OS package versions.

questions.q: How should code handle Databricks errors reliably?

options.t: By error condition or SQLSTATE
By line number in the stack trace
By the time the error happened
By matching the error message text

questions.explain: Every error has a condition, a SQLSTATE and a parameterized message; message text may change, so handle errors by condition or SQLSTATE.

questions.q: A query fails with TABLE_OR_VIEW_NOT_FOUND (42P01). Which checks help? (Choose two.)

options.t: Check the name and `current_schema()`
Qualify the name as catalog.schema.table
Restart the cluster
Grant MODIFY on the table
options.why: MODIFY doesn't make a table visible.

options.t: Run VACUUM

questions.explain: Check spelling and current_schema(), qualify catalog.schema.table, and check USE CATALOG/USE SCHEMA.

questions.q: A first cluster in a VNet-injected workspace never responds; the event log says the compute plane network is misconfigured. What is the likely cause?

options.t: Too few DBUs left in the subscription's quota for the first cluster
Routing or a firewall stops nodes reaching the control plane
The runtime is out of support
Unity Catalog isn't enabled

questions.explain: That message means routing or a firewall blocks the nodes: test connectivity from the subnet and check SSL inspection.

questions.q: How long is an LTS Databricks Runtime supported?

options.t: Six months
One year from the first release
Three years from GA
Ten years

questions.explain: A runtime gets about six months of feature releases; LTS versions get fixes for three years from GA.

questions.q: A developer can't commit to the default branch of a production repository. What does the Git folders guidance suggest?

options.t: Force-push from the workspace
Copy the notebook to a production folder by hand and commit it there
Ask an admin to disable branch protection
Commit to a branch and open a pull request in the Git provider

questions.explain: Without permission to commit to the default branch, create a branch and open a pull request in the Git provider; each developer works on their own branch.
